I've saved the analysis to `/work/answer.json`. All numbers came from a single Python run over `shop.db`.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment in Q3 by net sales | enterprise, 331,539,488 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid Q3 order | 249 |
| c. Top category in Q3 by net sales | acc, 234,478,195 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales (all time) | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refund total | u41@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid Q3 orders | 232 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 702,344 KRW |
| h. Net sales change, September vs August 2025 | -14.9% |

- **Duplicate accounts:** there are 300 customer accounts but only 250 distinct emails, so b, e and f count by email. Email case and whitespace were already consistent, so no extra cleanup was needed.
- **Segments:** these came in mixed case with stray spaces (e.g. " consumer", "Enterprise "). After trimming and lowercasing, they reduce to consumer, enterprise and smb.
- **Segment per order:** for question a, each order counts toward the segment of the account that placed it. If one email's accounts carry different segments, that person's sales can be split across segments. I didn't check whether this happens.
